normalized.result:
All three arrangements work. Screenshots under `prototypes/` (live: **http://maker:4001/statuses.html**). In every one, marking is the same: a **✓ Mark finished** button on a to-read item, and **↺ Move to To read** to reverse it. What differs is how you *see* the split:

**Arrangement A — Tabs** (`shot-22-status-tabs.png`)
Two tabs, **To read (3)** and **Finished (2)**, with a count on each. You look at one list at a time; the other is one click away. Cleanest and calmest — your main view shows only what's left to read.

**Arrangement B — One list with a switch + status badges** (`shot-23-status-segmented.png`)
A segmented control (**To read / Finished / All**) and every card carries a little **To read** / **Finished** badge. Finished items show struck-through. Lets you see *everything together* with an "All" view when you want the whole picture, while still filtering.

**Arrangement C — Two sections stacked** (`shot-24-status-sections.png`)
A single scrolling page with a **To read** section on top and a **Finished** section below. Everything is visible at once without switching, but a long list makes for a lot of scrolling.

Two questions:

1. **Which arrangement fits how you'd work — A (tabs, one at a time), B (one list with a filter + badges), or C (both sections on one page)?**
2. When you open the app, **which should you land on by default?** I'd assume **"To read"** is the natural home (that's the pile that needs attention), but tell me if you'd rather land on everything.
